Coining it at Kusile

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An exclusive expose on how construction companies at Kusile bribed senior managers to get contracts. Carte Blanche follows the money

Unique Selling Point:
We have documents that reveal front companies and shows the money flow from construction companies paying into front companies and those front companies paying for the
houses, a car and a chicken farms for Eskom senior managers. There have been very few exposes on Kusile as everyone who is coining it, keeps the secret.

Summary:
Kusile is way way over budget. The 2016 estimates excluding interest is that this megabuild project is at least R8 billion rand over budget, but it could be higher. Take away that debt and Eskom's debt that puts the country at risk would be a lot less. So what has gone wrong? Well it appears that everyone is coining it through bribery and corruption. Contractors pay Eskom management to get work and even Eskom employees have their own companies that get subcontracted to do work. Carte Blanche has proof that the chief engineer at Eskom subcontracts his own company for material that is provided free on site and gets paid millions.

Further information:
This is how it works. Carte Blanche has documents that reveal how big construction companies, one a listed company called Esor, paid millions into two front companies Mahamba transport and General enterprises, and Babinatlou Business services. That money was then laundered through these companies to pay for homes, farms and cars for suspended head of group capital Abram Masango and former project manager Frans Hlakudi. It appears that around R60 million rand may have flowed from construction company Tubular into one of his companies. We can show how he spent millions upgrading his chicken farms across Limpopo and Mpumalanga, and is now bragging that he is making a fortune.

There are over 200 contractors on site at Kusile and our sources say that many of them are paying bribes. We focus on only three companies and show how millions have been funnelled out in bribery, fraud and money laundering already. There is an investigation ongoing but according to our sources its going nowhere. Carte blanche has the case number but our sources say the police have been paid off and nothing has happened with the investigation.

Extra Budget Items:
May need a couple of extra days to get all the drone footage of the chicken farms and homes in Limpopo and Mpumalanga

Abram Masango
Frans hlakudi

gauteng, Mpumalanga and Limpo

Press Release:


Coining it on Kusile
How did an initial budget of R80-billion for the Kusile power station skyrocket to a projected R160-billion on completion? Construction that would have taken six years may now only be finished by 2022. We investigate secrets, lies and mind-boggling cost-overruns.


Script:


KUSILE FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 27th MAY 2018

Commentary One
Kusile power station began construction in 2008. It should have taken at most, six years to complete. Now ten years later, it will only be finished around 2022

Link
So, it's taken more than ten years to build this power station and its still not finished, and if you are wanting an answer why Eskom needs more money from you to remain a going concern, a big part of that answer lies right here, behind me.

Commentary Two
Kusile was Abram Masango's baby. This Eskom executive impressed the parliamentary committee on public enterprises, when he testified in February

Abram Masango
I was the project director for the Kusile project for approximately 8 years, before being promoted to the group executive

Commentary Three
When Masango testified, he was desperate to get his job back. He had been suspended on charges of corruption and conflict of interest

Masango
These are vague and unsubstantiated allegations which I deny in the strongest terms

Commentary Four
He blamed his former friend, Eskom's Matshela Koko, for the allegations, and claims that because of his role as a whistleblower, he was subjected to a campaign of harassment and intimidation, to the extent that his life was in grave danger.

Masango
I have no doubt that my suspension was an attempt to silence me, discredit me and undermine my credibility as a potential witness at Mr. Koko's disciplinary hearing.

Commentary Five
For 20 years, these friends rose up the ranks at Eskom. Both wanted the top job of CEO, but they fell out, when each accused the other, of corruption. Both professed absolute loyalty to Eskom.

Koko
For those who know me, I always say my blood is Eskom blue

Commentary Six
Koko, was exposed on Carte Blanche for the Optimum prepayment which at first, he denied. Later, he faced a disciplinary for his role in the Impulse international deal, as well as trying to remove Masango's close associates on Kusile. Koko was cleared, but he left Eskom under a cloud. Masango returned to work a few weeks ago after being cleared of all charges by a senior counsel

Masango
It goes without saying that my extensive knowledge and experience can only add value to the power utility at a time when it is in a major crisis.

Commentary seven
By November, Koko's reputation was in tatters, so when he alleged Masango was corrupt, no one was listening, except Money web journalist Antoinette Slabbert

Antoinette
I got some documents and what unfolded was a very strange and interesting story of Mr Koko trying to stop corruption at Kusile - which went totally contrary to the popular narrative at that stage

Commentary Eight
Now, a new forensic report commissioned by Eskom, reveals payments made, front companies, properties and vehicles, and how some of the biggest contractors on the Kusile construction site, tried to keep Eskom bosses, Abram Masango and France Hlakudi happy.

France Hlakudi ,whose image is absent from the internet was contracts manager under Masango.

Mandla
If Eskom is serious about corruption at Eskom the number one person to clean up is Abram Masango

Commentary ten
About two years ago, Mpumalanga activist, Mandla Bothman began to look into a company on Kusile called Vitrovian. Eskom had instructed Kusile Civil works, a joint venture between the big construction companies, to sign a service agreement with Vitrovian in 2011.

LINK
Vitrovian really hit the jackpot on Kusile- they were appointed to do community liaison work and for the last 7 years, R215 million has flowed to this company.

Commentary eleven
The report shows millions pouring in, each month.

Mandla
The big question is what is it that Eskom is paying Vitrovian to do? Why does Eskom keep paying these people, while they are doing nothing?

Commentary twelve
In their response, Vitrovian say they have not been officially shown the report ,and until such time as they have, they will not be commenting

Mandla
this is the company that is working hand in hand with Abram Masango. It's a looting tool. I will give you an example, the likes of the business expo, they are saying it's a business expo, the community must benefit, we are not. The Mandela day that is where they are looting a lot of money, the sports day, no one is benefitting, but they are enriching themselves

Commentary thirteen
He links threats to make him disappear, to Vitrovian.

Mandla
They said I must not be given any opportunity at Kusile, because I am a spy. I am not a spy - I am taking them hands on.

Commentary Fourteen
Everyone wanted a piece of the Kusile pie, including it seems, Abram Masango's former business partner, Arony Mahamba who is still in business with Masango's wife.

Devi Link
Mr Mahamba who has a transport company gets work here on Kusile. Substantial payments are made by Esor, Tubular and others to Mr Mahamba's company and guess what happens next? Mahamba transport pays R600 000 deposit on Masango's new Mercedes Benz.

Commentary fifteen
They said they did not want to deal with our questions claiming confidential contracts

Masango also claims he has saved Eskom money

Masango
During my tenure at Eskom I successfully managed many projects for the financial benefit of Eskom.

Commentary sixteen
But is that really true? Because the three mega projects under his control, Ingula, Kusile and Medupi ,have all come in over budget and over time. Way over! As Infrastructure economist, Dr. Grove Steyn explains.

Devi
Let's go back to the very beginning how much was Kusile going to cost the taxpayer?
Dr. Grove Steyn
Some of the earliest budget estimates was for R80 billion, the last numbers from Eskom is that it's now going to cost R161 billion, and I expect that budget to increase

Commentary seventeen
And says Steyn, due to excess capacity, we don't really need Kusile right now



Devi
I would think it's going to be a whopper with interest?
Dr. Grove Steyn
Based on information we get from Eskom our understanding is that Kusile in 2017 rand's will cost R226 billion rand

Commentary eighteen
Consider this, Eskom is asking us to fill a R66 billion hole, but if Masango's projects had come in even modestly over budget, Eskom would not have had to go begging to NERSA to increase its tariffs. Now, all Eskom's new CEO Phakamani Hadebe can do, is stem the looting.

Phakamani Hadebe
We told the investors that we continue to do the investigations and we are taking decisions whenever we find wrong doing. We continue to review the contracts 5000 of them and we have covered a lot of ground

Commentary nineteen
The SIU is also investigating maladministration, and any losses or prejudice suffered by Eskom on Ingula, Medupi and Kusile. Meanwhile Eskom has begun to do lifestyle audits.

Up sound Music

France Hlakudi who resigned a few months ago, may have been a good place to start, because clearly he has a friend in Tenova mining. Their one contract to construct a conveyer system, doubled to R2.1 billion rand and someone had to sign off those increases.

Could that explain, why Tenova paid for his family holiday in December?

Up sound Caribbean music

And agreed to his wife's request for business class tickets from Johannesburg to Charles De Gaulle and back.

DEVI LINK
Tenova mining said they were surprised by our letter when we asked them why they had paid for a holiday for France Hlakudi and his family. They never answered the question but then again how do you explain that you paid for the contracts manager on Kusile to spend 19 days on the French Caribbean?!

Commentary twenty
This dam, hidden on a farm in the middle of nowhere was built by Esor. Why?

Up sound co- ordinates

They have a contract to build the underground terraces on Kusile in Mpumalanga, and that would surely not include a dam on France Hlakudi's private chicken farm in Limpopo. But this listed company was sending emails to France asking if he was happy with the construction.

Their price to Eskom ballooned from R342 million to R1.9 billion. Perhaps they needed their variation orders approved.

Devi
How are you, I need to see Wessel Van Zyl

Commentary twenty- one
CEO Wessel Van Zyl sent us an email and said that at all times Esor has acted legally and properly in its conduct at Kusile and vehemently denies any allegations of assistance to Eskom Employees. He offered no explanation for the dam.

Esor may also struggle to explain why they paid over a million rand to Masango's accountant company, who in turn paid for the chicken house curtains on France Hlakudi's farm.

Chickens

So indirectly your electricity tariff is paying for chicken house curtains via a listed construction company!

DEVI LINK
Behind me is Tubular construction. They managed to get the contract to build the last 3 huge air- cooled condensers on Kusile. These are like large radiators

Commentary twenty- two
In 2015 Tubular was in financial trouble, the report finds that it did not benefit Eskom to give Tubular the contract, yet Masango and Hlakudi recommended that Eskom should remove the contract from Alstom and give it to Tubular

Antoinette
In short, they kicked out Alstom, and Eskom started dealing directly with Tubular
Devi
But how do you get a contractor out?
Antoinette
You pay him the profit he would have made. Eskom paid Alstom the profit it would have made had it completed the contract , in other words you don't do the job, but you get the profit, so there is no risk

Commentary Twenty- three
In an affidavit ,a Tubular whistleblower says the plan was to keep the initial price low so Hlakudi could sign the contract. Tubular would later create false claims or variation orders to generate new income to R1.5 billion rand - and that is almost exactly what happened

Antoinette
That contract at R700 million, two years later that was increased to R1.2 billion

Commentary Twenty-Four
Masango says he supported the decision to de scope Tubular, which he says was made by various committees and the Eskom board. He claims the decision was to avoid claims totaling R56 billion against Eskom as well as retrenchments by Tubular.

What is more difficult to explain, is why Tubular paid R20 million into Hlakudi's business account, Hlakudi translation services, after the deal was concluded

Devi
How do we know that Frans Hlakudi was benefitting from this contract in the end?
Antoinette
Well we saw bank statements/ to give you an idea in one month in 2015 there was R500 000 withdrawn in cash, in 2016 in May there was R3 million cash in total withdrawn

Commentary Twenty- Five
The report notes that after Tubular was awarded the contract, Masango and Hlakudi made substantial payments towards the purchase price of various properties, and Hlakudi renovated his home at a cost of R7.6 million

Devi Link
Tubular denies paying any bribes. In this letter to us they say that the overwhelming conclusion is that none of Tubulars social upliftment activities can be classified as a bribe.

Commentary Twenty-six
Hlaukudi also denies all the allegations against him including any impropriety in his dealings with Tubular. He says he made full disclosure to Eskom of his outside interests and allegations against him were part of smear campaign. Since he left Eskom, Hlakudi is expanding his chicken empire and there is speculation that Abram Masango may soon be promoted.

THE END 13 minutes and 4 seconds.

PROMO TWO 15
The startling cost escalation on Kusile power station
Dr. Grove Steyn
the last numbers from Eskom is that it's now going to cost R161 billion, and I expect that budget to increase

PROMO THREE 10 seconds
Why did a prominent construction company working on Kusile, pay for a Caribbean holiday for a former Eskom executive?

PROMO FOUR 30 ''

Commentary
Consider this, Eskom is asking us to fill a R66 billion hole, but if Medupi, Kusile and Ingula had come in on budget, Eskom wouldn't have had to go begging to NERSA to increase its tariffs. Now, all Eskom's new CEO Phakamani Hadebe can do, is stem the looting.

Phakamani Hadebe

These are like large radiators Commentary twenty- two In 2015 Tubular was in financial trouble, the report finds that it did not benefit Eskom to give Tubular the contract, yet Masango and Hlakudi recommended that Eskom should remove the contract from Alstom and give it to Tubular Antoinette In short, they kicked out Alstom, and Eskom started dealing directly with Tubular Devi But how do you get a contractor out? Antoinette You pay him the profit he would have made. Eskom paid Alstom the profit it would have made had it completed the contract , in other words you don't do the job, but you get the profit, so there is no risk Commentary Twenty- three In an affidavit ,a Tubular whistleblower says the plan was to keep the initial price low so Hlakudi could sign the contract. Tubular would later create false claims or variation orders to generate new income to R1.5 billion rand - and that is almost exactly what happened Antoinette That contract at R700 million, two years later that was increased to R1.2 billion Commentary Twenty-Four Masango says he supported the decision to de scope Tubular, which he says was made by various committees and the Eskom board. He claims the decision was to avoid claims totaling R56 billion against Eskom as well as retrenchments by Tubular. What is more difficult to explain, is why Tubular paid R20 million into Hlakudi's business account, Hlakudi translation services, after the deal was concluded Devi How do we know that Frans Hlakudi was benefitting from this contract in the end? Antoinette Well we saw bank statements/ to give you an idea in one month in 2015 there was R500 000 withdrawn in cash, in 2016 in May there was R3 million cash in total withdrawn Commentary Twenty- Five The report notes that after Tubular was awarded the contract, Masango and Hlakudi made substantial payments towards the purchase price of various properties, and Hlakudi renovated his home at a cost of R7.6 million Devi Link Tubular denies paying any bribes. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An exclusive expose on how construction companies at Kusile bribed senior managers to get contracts. Carte Blanche follows the money
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have documents that reveal front companies and shows the money flow from construction companies paying into front companies and those front companies paying for the houses, a car and a chicken farms for Eskom senior managers. There have been very few exposes on Kusile as everyone who is coining it, keeps the secret.
metadata.Summary: Kusile is way way over budget. The 2016 estimates excluding interest is that this megabuild project is at least R8 billion rand over budget, but it could be higher. Take away that debt and Eskom's debt that puts the country at risk would be a lot less. So what has gone wrong? Well it appears that everyone is coining it through bribery and corruption. Contractors pay Eskom management to get work and even Eskom employees have their own companies that get subcontracted to do work. Carte Blanche has proof that the chief engineer at Eskom subcontracts his own company for material that is provided free on site and gets paid millions.
metadata.Further information: This is how it works. Carte Blanche has documents that reveal how big construction companies, one a listed company called Esor, paid millions into two front companies Mahamba transport and General enterprises, and Babinatlou Business services. That money was then laundered through these companies to pay for homes, farms and cars for suspended head of group capital Abram Masango and former project manager Frans Hlakudi. It appears that around R60 million rand may have flowed from construction company Tubular into one of his companies. We can show how he spent millions upgrading his chicken farms across Limpopo and Mpumalanga, and is now bragging that he is making a fortune. There are over 200 contractors on site at Kusile and our sources say that many of them are paying bribes. We focus on only three companies and show how millions have been funnelled out in bribery, fraud and money laundering already. There is an investigation ongoing but according to our sources its going nowhere. Carte blanche has the case number but our sources say the police have been paid off and nothing has happened with the investigation.
